parameters.content:
## Workflow/Asset Backup to GitHub

### How it works

1. Runs daily. Pulls every workflow currently in this n8n instance via its own REST API, and pulls every n8n Variable (your firm's configuration values).
2. Commits each workflow as its own JSON file, and all variables as one file, to a GitHub repository you control -- updating the existing file if one is already there, so history/version tracking comes for free through Git.
3. If anything fails to back up, staff get an alert email naming exactly what failed -- a silent backup failure is worse than no backup at all.

**Credentials are never backed up.** n8n's own API already strips credential secrets from workflow exports, and this workflow does not touch the credentials API at all -- only workflow definitions and variables.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Create a private GitHub repository to hold the backups (e.g. `yourfirm/n8n-backups`).
- [ ] Generate an n8n API key from this same instance's Settings -> n8n API, and configure the 'n8n API (self)' credential with header name `X-N8N-API-KEY`.
- [ ] Generate a GitHub Personal Access Token with `Contents: write` scope on the backup repo, and configure the 'GitHub API (backup PAT)' credential with header name `Authorization` and value `Bearer <token>`.
- [ ] Set the required n8n Variables: N8N_INSTANCE_URL, GITHUB_BACKUP_REPO, FIRM_STAFF_EMAIL.
- [ ] Activate the workflow.

## Back up every workflow

Fetches every workflow from this n8n instance and commits each one as its own JSON file to GitHub, updating in place if it already exists.

## Back up variables (configuration)

Fetches every n8n Variable and commits them all as a single JSON file to GitHub -- never the credentials themselves.

## Summary and failure alert

Waits for both backup branches to finish, then alerts staff only if something actually failed.

nodes.name: Run Daily Backup
nodes.notes: Runs once a day, off-hours by default (3am). Adjust the cron expression to whatever time suits your firm.

nodes.name: Fetch All Workflows From n8n
nodes.notes: Calls this SAME n8n instance's own REST API -- N8N_INSTANCE_URL should point right back at this instance. A limit of 250 covers a solo/small firm's full workflow count in one page; raise it if you have more.

nodes.name: Split Out Workflow List
nodes.notes: One item per workflow currently in this n8n instance.

nodes.name: Build GitHub File For Workflow
nodes.notes: One backup file per workflow, named from the workflow's own name and ID so it stays stable even if you rename it later.

nodes.name: Fetch Existing Workflow File SHA
nodes.notes: GitHub requires the current file's SHA to update it in place -- a 404 here just means this workflow has never been backed up before.

nodes.name: Parse Existing Workflow File SHA
nodes.notes: Reads the file-build data by name, not $json, since the GitHub lookup in between replaces $json with its own response.

nodes.name: Commit Workflow To GitHub
nodes.notes: Creates the file if it's new, or updates it in place (via the SHA) if it already exists -- Git keeps the version history either way.

nodes.name: Parse Workflow Commit Result
nodes.notes: Reads the pre-commit data by name, not $json, since the GitHub commit call in between replaces $json with its own response. A failed commit here is surfaced, never silently ignored.

nodes.name: Aggregate All Workflow Backup Results
nodes.notes: Collects every workflow's backup result into one list so the summary step can check for any failures across the whole set.

nodes.name: Fetch All n8n Variables
nodes.notes: Backs up your firm's configuration values (the same N8N Variables used across every template in this catalog) -- never credentials, which n8n's API does not expose.

nodes.name: Build GitHub File For Variables
nodes.notes: All variables go in a single file -- there's no reason to split configuration values across multiple files the way workflows are split.

nodes.name: Fetch Existing Variables File SHA
nodes.notes: A 404 here just means variables have never been backed up before.

nodes.name: Parse Existing Variables File SHA
nodes.notes: Reads the file-build data by name, not $json, since the GitHub lookup in between replaces $json with its own response.

nodes.name: Commit Variables To GitHub
nodes.notes: Creates the file if it's new, or updates it in place if it already exists.

nodes.name: Parse Variables Commit Result
nodes.notes: Reads the pre-commit data by name, not $json, since the GitHub commit call in between replaces $json with its own response.

nodes.name: Merge Workflow And Variable Backup Results
nodes.notes: Waits for both the workflow backups and the variables backup to finish before building one combined summary.

nodes.name: Build Backup Summary
nodes.notes: One combined view of the whole backup run -- how many workflows succeeded, whether variables backed up, and exactly what failed if anything did.

nodes.name: If Any Backup Failed
nodes.notes: Staff only get emailed when something actually needs attention -- a fully successful daily backup stays silent.

nodes.name: Build Backup Failure Alert Email
nodes.notes: Names exactly what failed -- staff shouldn't have to dig through execution logs to find out.

nodes.name: Send Backup Failure Alert Email
nodes.notes: Internal alert only -- a failed backup is an ops problem for staff, not something a client ever sees.

nodes.name: Skip — No Backup Failures
nodes.notes: Everything backed up cleanly -- nothing further to do today.
